q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
These are the Aayaat of the Qur'aan and of the clear Book.
v.s: Tā, Seen. These are the verses of the Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] and a clear Book
v.c: Ṭâ-Sĩn. These are the verses of the Quran; the clear Book.

q: guidance and a carrier of good news for the Mu'mineen
(informing them about the blessings and rewards they will receive)...
v.s: As guidance and good tidings for the believers
v.c: ˹It is˺ a guide and good news for the believers:

q: (perform it regularly with all its etiquette),
v.s: Who establish prayer and give zakāh, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith].
v.c: ˹those˺ who establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.

q: As for those who do not believe in the Aakhirah, We have beautified their
acts for them, so they wander blindly
(committing more evil without realising that they are accountable and will soon be taken to task for the evil they do).
v.s: Indeed, for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made pleasing to them their deeds, so they wander blindly.
v.c: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have certainly made their ˹evil˺ deeds appealing to them, so they wander blindly.

q: For such people there shall be a terrible punishment and they will be the worst losers in the Aakhirah.
v.s: Those are the ones for whom there will be the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers.
v.c: It is they who will suffer a dreadful torment, and in the Hereafter they will ˹truly˺ be the greatest losers.

q: Undoubtedly, you are given the Qur'aan from the Wise, the All Knowing
(Who knows exactly what man requires and Who will therefore provide him with exactly what he needs in the Qur'aan).
v.s: And indeed, [O Muhammad], you re- ceive the Qur’ān from one Wise and Knowing.
v.c: And indeed, you ˹O Prophet˺ are receiving the Quran from the One ˹Who is˺ All-Wise, All-Knowing.

q: When Moosa ﵊ said to his family
(his wife, after they lost their way en route to Egypt),
“I notice a fire. I shall shortly bring you some news
(directions from the people at the fire)
or a burning stake so that you may warm yourselves.”
v.s: [Mention] when Moses said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there information or will bring you a burning torch that you may warm yourselves."
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when Moses said to his family, “I have spotted a fire. I will either bring you some directions from there, or a burning torch so you may warm yourselves.”

q: (which was not really afire, but a bright radiance covering a tree),
and those in the vicinity of the fire
Allaah, the Rabb of the universe is Pure
v.s: But when he came to it, he was called, "Blessed is whoever is at the fire and whoever is around it. And exalted is God, Lord of the worlds.
v.c: But when he came to it, he was called ˹by Allah˺, “Blessed is the one at the fire, and whoever is around it! Glory be to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.

v.s: O Moses, indeed it is I - God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
v.c: O Moses! It is truly I. I am Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.

q: (he threw it down, it turned into a snake and when)
Moosa ﵊ saw the staff moving rapidly like a snake, he
(was naturally afraid and to save himself, he)
stepped back on his heels without looking back.
“O Moosa! Do not fear. Indeed, the Ambiyaa have no fear in My presence...”
v.s: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [God said], "O Moses, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear.
v.c: Now, throw down your staff!” But when he saw it slithering like a snake, he ran away without looking back. ˹Allah reassured him,˺ “O Moses! Do not be afraid! Messengers should have no fear in My presence.

q: ...except the one who had done wrong
(because he fears that I may take him to task for it, he)
Verily I am the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful
(and will forgive him, thereby dispelling his fear of being punished).” (Allaah then instructed Moosa ﵊ to grab hold of the snake, after which Allaah transformed it back into a staff.)
v.s: Otherwise, he who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil - indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful.
v.c: ˹Fear is˺ only for those who do wrong. But if they later mend ˹their˺ evil ˹ways˺ with good, then I am certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

q: (Demonstrating another miracle to Moosa ﵊, Allaah commanded him further saying,)
“Put your hand into your collar, it will emerge shining white
(the light will not be because of any disease).
These two are among the nine Aayaat
with which you will go to
(to prove to them that you are My Rasool).
They are certainly a disobedient nation
v.s: And put your hand into the opening of your garment [at the breast]; it will come out white without disease. [These are] among the nine signs [you will take] to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient."
v.c: Now put your hand through ˹the opening of˺ your collar, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished. ˹These are two˺ of nine signs for Pharaoh and his people. They have truly been a rebellious people.”

q: came to them as eye-openers, they
(Fir'oun and his people refused to believe them because of their arrogance and they)
v.s: But when there came to them Our visible signs, they said, "This is obvious magic."
v.c: But when Our enlightening signs came to them, they said, “This is pure magic.”

q: They unjustly and arrogantly rejected them
whereas their souls were convinced about them
(they knew deep down in their hearts that these miracles were definitely from Allaah, but their arrogance did not allow them to admit it).
So see what was the outcome of those who caused corruption
(Fir'oun and his entire army were all destroyed when they drowned in the sea).
v.s: And they rejected them, while their [inner] selves were convinced thereof, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
v.c: And, although their hearts were convinced the signs were true, they still denied them wrongfully and arrogantly. See then what was the end of the corruptors!

q: (about how to give passing sound judgement)
Sulaymaan ﵊. They both said, “All praise is due to Allaah Who has favoured us more than many of His bondsmen who have Imaan
(by granting us Prophethood, wisdom and kingdom).'
v.s: And We had certainly given to David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise [is due] to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants."
v.c: Indeed, We granted knowledge to David and Solomon. And they said ˹in acknowledgment˺, “All praise is for Allah Who has privileged us over many of His faithful servants.”

q: (as Nabi and king of the Bani Israa'eel)
have been taught the speech of the birds and have been granted everything
(that is granted to the Ambiyaa ﵊ and to kings).
This is certainly a manifest bounty
v.s: And Solomon inherited David. He said, "O people, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty."
v.c: And David was succeeded by Solomon, who said, “O people! We have been taught the language of birds, and been given everything ˹we need˺. This is indeed a great privilege.”

q: Sulaymaan ﵊ army of Jinn, men and birds were gathered for him
(so many in number that they had to be)
(so that order may be maintained among their ranks).
v.s: And gathered for Solomon were his soldiers of the jinn and men and birds, and they were [marching] in rows
v.c: Solomon’s forces of jinn, humans, and birds were rallied for him, perfectly organized.

q: Until, when they reached a valley of ants, an ant announced, “O ants! Enter your dwellings so that Sulaymaan ﵊ and his army
(that they are trampling on you because you are almost invisible to them and they do not have knowledge of the unseen).”
v.s: Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Solomon and his soldiers while they perceive not."
v.c: And when they came across a valley of ants, an ant warned, “O ants! Go quickly into your homes so Solomon and his armies do not crush you, unknowingly.”

q: (Amused at the intelligence of the ant,)
began to smile and then laughed at her
speech saying, “O my Rabb! Allow me to express gratitude for Your bounty
(for enabling me to understand the language of the ants),
which You have granted me and my parents, and
to perform good actions that You are pleased with. And, out of Your Mercy, include me among Your righteous bondsmen.”
v.s: So [Solomon] smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the ranks of] Your righteous servants."
v.c: So Solomon smiled in amusement at her words, and prayed, “My Lord! Inspire me to ˹always˺ be thankful for Your favours which You have blessed me and my parents with, and to do good deeds that please you. Admit me, by Your mercy, into ˹the company of˺ Your righteous servants.”

q: (of his army and could not find a bird called Hudhud)
he said, “Why do I not see Hudhud
v.s: And he took attendance of the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe - or is he among the absent?
v.c: ˹One day˺ he inspected the birds, and wondered, “Why is it that I cannot see the hoopoe? Or could he be absent?

q: (When Sulaymaan ﵊ discovered that Hudhud was absent without leave, he said,)
“I shall surely punish him severely or slaughter him unless he comes to me with a proper explanation.”
v.s: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him unless he brings me clear authorization."
v.c: I will surely subject him to a severe punishment, or ˹even˺ slaughter him, unless he brings me a compelling excuse.”

m: and I have come to you
q: It was only a short while thereafter when Hudhud
(arrived and, presenting his reason for being away, he)
knowledge of something about which you have no knowledge. I have just returned from Saba
v.s: But he [i.e., the hoopoe] stayed not long and said, "I have encompassed [in knowledge] that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news.
v.c: It was not long before the bird came and said, “I have found out something you do not know. I have just come to you from Sheba with sure news.

q: (a queen by the name of Bilqis)
(that other rulers have eg wealth, weapons, beauty etc). (In addition to this,)
v.s: Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.
v.c: Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, who has been given everything ˹she needs˺, and who has a magnificent throne.

q: “I found her and her people prostrating to
the sun instead of Allaah. Shaytaan has
prevented them from the right path
because of which they are not rightly guided
(and are steeped in shirk so wage Jihaad against them).”
v.s: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from [His] way, so they are not guided,
v.c: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah. For Satan has made their deeds appealing to them—hindering them from the ˹Right˺ Way and leaving them unguided—

q: “They do not prostrate before Allaah, Who
can expose the hidden things in the heavens and the earth, and who knows what you hide and what you disclose
(and Who is therefore most worthy of being Worshipped).”
v.s: [And] so they do not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare -
v.c: so they do not prostrate to Allah, Who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you ˹all˺ conceal and what you reveal.

q: “Allaah is the One besides Whom there is no other Ilaah. He is the Rabb of the glorious throne
(which is far superior to any throne of this world).” (One who recites or hears this verse being recited must perform Sajdah.)
v.s: God - there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne."
v.c: ˹He is˺ Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”

q: “We shall soon see whether you have spoken the truth or whether you are from the liars.”
(Even the bird was given a fair trial.)
v.s: [Solomon] said, "We will see whether you were truthful or were of the liars.
v.c: Solomon said, “We will see whether you are telling the truth or lying.

q: “Take this letter of mine and throw
and see what reply they give.”
v.s: Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them. Then leave them and see what [answer] they will return."
v.c: Go with this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then stand aside and see how they will respond.”

q: (When Hudhud dropped the letter into the queen's lap, she opened it, read its contents and)
said, “O ministers! An honourable letter has been thrown
v.s: She said, "O eminent ones, indeed, to me has been delivered a noble letter.
v.c: The Queen ˹later˺ announced, “O chiefs! Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me.

q: (“I begin with the name of Allaah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”).
v.s: Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it is [i.e., reads]: 'In the name of God, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,
v.c: It is from Solomon, and it reads: ‘In the Name of Allah—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.

q: and come to me in submission
(obedience).'” (Sulaymaan ﵊ summoned them so that he could convey to them the message of Towheed.)
v.s: Be not haughty with me but come to me in submission [as Muslims].'"
v.c: Do not be arrogant with me, but come to me, fully submitting ˹to Allah˺.’”

q: She said, “O ministers! Advise me in my matter, for I shall never decide any matter until you are present with me
v.s: She said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness [for] me."
v.c: She said, “O chiefs! Advise me in this matter of mine, for I would never make any decision without you.”

q: They replied, “We are people of great
(and are therefore prepared to fight Sulaymaan),
the decision rests with you. Therefore you decide what commands you wish to issue.
('We will support you in any decision you make).”
v.s: They said, "We are men of strength and of great military might, but the command is yours, so see what you will command."
v.c: They responded, “We are a people of strength and great ˹military˺ might, but the decision is yours, so decide what you will command.”

q: She said, “Verily when kings enter any town
its noble people. This is what they
v.s: She said, “Indeed kings - when they enter a city, they ruin it and render the honoured of its people humbled. And thus do they do.
v.c: She reasoned, “Indeed, when kings invade a land, they ruin it and debase its nobles. They really do so!

q: “(Let us therefore take no drastic action until we ascertain their strength and know whether Sulaymaan ﵊ is a Nabi or just another king. To discover all of this,)
to them and then see with what
(If Sulaymaan refuses to accept the gift, he must certainly be a Nabi, otherwise not.)
v.s: But indeed, I will send to them a gift and see with what [reply] the messengers will return."
v.c: But I will certainly send him a gift, and see what ˹response˺ my envoys will return with.”

q: (I have no need for your wealth because)
my Rabb has given me is better than what He has given you. It is you people who are pleased about your gift
(because you have love for the treasures of this world, while I do not. I do not want your wealth, but desire that you become Mu'mineen).”
v.s: So when they came to Solomon, he said, "Do you provide me with wealth? But what God has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift.
v.c: When the chief-envoy came to him, Solomon said, “Do you offer me wealth? What Allah has granted me is far greater than what He has granted you. No! It is you who rejoice in ˹receiving˺ gifts.

m: surely, we will come to them
and surely, we will drive them out
q: (with the gift). (Tell them that if they refuse to submit,)
We shall certainly march against them with an army
that they will have no defence against it. We shall then certainly
in shame, while they are humbled
(defeated).” (When the message reached the queen and her people, they decided to comply with Sulaymaan's instruction and they left for his kingdom.)
v.s: Return to them, for we will surely come to them with soldiers that they will be powerless to encounter, and we will surely expel them therefrom in humiliation, and they will be debased."
v.c: Go back to them, for we will certainly mobilize against them forces which they can never resist, and we will drive them out from there in disgrace, fully humbled.”

q: Which of you can bring her throne to me before they come to us in submission
v.s: [Solomon] said, "O assembly [of jinn], which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"
v.c: Solomon asked, “O chiefs! Which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me in ˹full˺ submission?”

q: A giant of the Jinn said, “I shall bring it to you before you stand up from your place
v.s: A powerful one from among the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [task] strong and trustworthy."
v.c: One mighty jinn responded, “I can bring it to you before you rise from this council of yours. And I am quite strong and trustworthy for this ˹task˺.”

q: (whose identity cannot be proven beyond doubt)
who possessed knowledge of the Book
“(Before you stand up from your place is a long time because)
I shall bring it to you before you can even blink your eye.”
(True to his word, the throne was present before the batting of an eye and)
saw it placed firmly in his presence, he said, “This is from the grace
of my Rabb to test whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. Whoever is grateful shows gratitude only for his own good
(because he will receive the benefit of showing gratitude). (On the other hand),
Whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Rabb is Independent
(and can easily bestow the same favours on others).”
v.s: Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when [Solomon] saw it placed before him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."
v.c: But the one who had knowledge of the Scripture said, “I can bring it to you in the blink of an eye.” So when Solomon saw it placed before him, he exclaimed, “This is by the grace of my Lord to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, it is only for their own good. But whoever is ungrateful, surely my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Most Generous.”

q: her throne for her so that we may see whether she is rightly guided
(whether she is intelligent enough to recognise her throne)
or from among those who are not guided aright.”
(In this manner, it may be ascertained whether she will be able to understand the message of Towheed or not.)
v.s: He said, "Disguise for her her throne; we will see whether she will be guided [to truth] or will be of those who is not guided."
v.c: ˹Then˺ Solomon said, “Disguise her throne for her so we may see whether she will recognize ˹it˺ or she will not be able to.”

q: When she arrived, she was asked, “Is your throne something like this?” She replied, “It seems like this is the very one. We were informed from before
(we arrived that you are Allaah's Rasool)
v.s: So when she arrived, it was said [to her], "Is your throne like this?" She said, "[It is] as though it was it." [Solomon said], "And we were given knowledge before her, and we have been Muslims [in submission to God].
v.c: So when she arrived, it was said ˹to her˺, “Is your throne like this?” She replied, “It looks to be the same. We have ˹already˺ received knowledge ˹of Solomon’s prophethood˺ before this ˹miracle˺, and have submitted ˹to Allah˺.”

q: (The above proved that she was an intelligent woman, but)
What she worshipped instead of Allaah
(had grown accustomed to worshipping the sun because she)
was from a nation of Kaafiroon
(and had not received the message of Towheed earlier).
v.s: And that which she was worshipping other than God had averted her [from submission to Him]. Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people."
v.c: But she had been hindered by what she used to worship instead of Allah, for she was indeed from a disbelieving people.

q: (To prove to her that man cannot depend only on his intelligence and senses and needs divine guidance,)
“Enter the palace.” When she saw it
she thought it was a pool of deep water and exposed her calf
(as she lifted her dress to wade through the water).
(to her), “(This is not a pool of water but)
It is a palace that is constructed
(built over water, which is so clear that the glass is almost invisible and only the water can be seen).” (Realising that she needed guidance from Allaah)
She said, “O my Rabb! I have surely oppressed my soul
(by worshipping the sun which, according to my intelligence and senses, seemed to be the greatest power). (However,)
submit with Sulaymaan ﵊ to Allaah, the Rabb of the universe
(because I realise that my intelligence and my senses alone cannot tell me everything and they often deceive me).”
v.s: She was told, "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water and uncovered her shins [to wade through]. He said, "Indeed, it is a palace [whose floor is] made smooth with glass." She said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds."
v.c: Then she was told, “Enter the palace.” But when she saw the hall, she thought it was a body of water, so she bared her legs. Solomon said. “It is just a palace paved with crystal.” ˹At last˺ she declared, “My Lord! I have certainly wronged my soul. Now I ˹fully˺ submit myself along with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.” Prophet Ṣâliḥ and His People

q: We had certainly sent to the
“Worship Allaah.” However, they suddenly became two rival groups
(when one group accepted his message while another group opposed him).
v.s: And We had certainly sent to Thamūd their brother Sālih, [saying], “Worship God,” and at once they were two parties conflicting.
v.c: And We certainly sent to the people of Thamûd their brother Ṣâliḥ, proclaiming, “Worship Allah,” but they suddenly split into two opposing groups.

q: He said, “O my people! Why do you seek to hasten evil before good
(by asking for Allaah's punishment instead of asking for safety)?
Why do you not seek forgiveness from Allaah
so that mercy may be shown to you
(and you may be saved from punishment)?”
v.s: He said, "O my people, why are you impatient for evil before [i.e., instead of] good? Why do you not seek forgiveness of God that you may receive mercy?"
v.c: He urged ˹the disbelieving group˺, “O my people! Why do you ˹seek to˺ hasten the torment rather than grace? If only you sought Allah’s forgiveness so you may be shown mercy!”

m: We consider you a bad omen
We consider you a bad omen
q: from you and from those with you.” He said, “Your predictions of evil
(Only He can bring you the evil you expect from us.)
You are but a nation that is being tested
(to see whether you will do good by accepting Imaan or whether you will remain on kufr and suffer the consequences).'
v.s: They said, "We consider you a bad omen, you and those with you." He said, "Your omen [i.e., fate] is with God. Rather, you are a people being tested."
v.c: They replied, “You and your followers are a bad omen for us.” He responded, “Your omens are destined by Allah. In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people being tested.” An Attempt on Ṣâliḥ’s Life

q: There were nine persons in the town
in the land and never made amends
v.s: And there were in the city nine family heads causing corruption in the land and not amending [its affairs].
v.c: And there were in the city nine ˹elite˺ men who spread corruption in the land, never doing what is right.

m: surely, we will attack him by night
q: “You should all swear an oath by Allaah that we will all secretly kill him
at night, after which we shall tell his successors
'We were not present at the place where his family was killed
(and therefore know nothing about the murders),
v.s: They said, "Take a mutual oath by God that we will kill him by night, he and his family. Then we will say to his executor, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.'"
v.c: They vowed, “Let us swear by Allah that we will take him and his family down by night. Then we will certainly say to his ˹closest˺ heirs, ‘We did not witness the murder of his family. We are definitely telling the truth.’”

q: (to destroy the Kuffaar and save the Mu'mineen)
(When mischief reaches such limits, destruction of the mischief makers soon follows.)
v.s: And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not.
v.c: And ˹so˺ they made a plan, but We too made a plan, while they were unaware.

q: So see what was the outcome
v.s: Then look how was the outcome of their plan - that We destroyed them and their people, all.
v.c: See then what the consequences of their plan were: We ˹utterly˺ destroyed them and their people all together.

q: that lie in ruins because of their oppression
There is definitely an Aayah in this for people with knowledge
v.s: So those are their houses, desolate because of the wrong they had done. Indeed in that is a sign for people who know.
v.c: So their homes are there, ˹but completely˺ ruined because of their wrongdoing. Surely in this is a lesson for people of knowledge.

q: those who had Imaan and who adopted Taqwa.
v.s: And We saved those who believed and used to fear God.
v.c: And We delivered those who were faithful and were mindful ˹of Allah˺.

q: (as a Nabi to his nation). (Remember the time)
When he told them, “Do you behave immorally
(while actually looking on at your despicable homosexual activities)?”
v.s: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality while you are seeing?
v.c: And ˹remember˺ Lot, when he rebuked ˹the men of˺ his people, “Do you commit that shameful deed while you can see ˹one another˺?

q: (This is too contemptible to even imagine!)
You are but a nation that behaves ignorantly.”
v.s: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly."
v.c: Do you really lust after men instead of women? In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people acting ignorantly.”

q: (Knowing that they were guilty of a dreadful crime against morality and human nature,)
The only reply that his people could give was, “Expel the family of Loot ﵊ from your town. They are people who merely wish
v.s: But the answer of his people was not except that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."
v.c: But his people’s only response was to say, “Expel Lot’s followers from your land! They are a people who wish to remain chaste!”

q: (when they refused to accept his message inspire of respected warnings, We punished them and)
except his wife. We had destined that she should be among those left behind
(to die of the punishment because she was one of the Kuffaar).
v.s: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; We destined her to be of those who remained behind.
v.c: So We delivered him and his family, except his wife. We had destined her to be one of the doomed.

q: on them. Evil indeed was the shower of those who were
v.s: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
v.c: And We poured upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺. How evil was the rain of those who had been warned!

q: (for destroying those who are a scourge to mankind)
and peace be on those bondsmen of His whom He has chosen
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “Praise be to God, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is God better or what they associate with Him?”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the servants He has chosen.” ˹Ask the disbelievers,˺ “Which is better: Allah or whatever ˹gods˺ they associate ˹with Him˺?”
v.h: Questions to the Pagans:1) Who Is the Creator?

q: Who has created the heavens and the earth and has sent rain for you from the sky
(not better than the gods of Mushrikeen)?
beauty. It is not possible for you
(all man can do is plant a seed. He then has no control over the rest of the process).
Is there another Ilaah with Allaah? No,
(no one else can be worthy of worship but He because no one can accomplish these feats. However,)
(refuse to accept Towheed and therefore continue to)
v.s: [More precisely], is He [not best] who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you rain from the sky, causing to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty which you could not [otherwise] have grown the trees thereof? Is there a deity with God? [No], but they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him].
v.c: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down rain for you from the sky, by which We cause delightful gardens to grow? You could never cause their trees to grow. Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But they are a people who set up equals ˹to Allah˺!

q: He Who made the earth stable
(solid so that it does not shake or tilt),
Who created rivers in its midst, Who placed mountains on it, and Who has placed a barrier between the two seas
(is He not better than the gods of Mushrikeen)?
(there can never be another being with superior powers who deserves to be worshipped),
(people who do not want to understand Towheed).
v.s: Is He [not best] who made the earth a stable ground and placed within it rivers and made for it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with God? [No], but most of them do not know.
v.c: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who made the earth a place of settlement, caused rivers to flow through it, placed firm mountains upon it, and set a barrier between ˹fresh and salt˺ bodies of water? Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But most of them do not know.

q: He Who responds to the distressed
(not better than the gods of Mushrikeen)?
(However, despite the advice that comes to you Mushrikeen,)
v.s: Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth? Is there a deity with God? Little do you remember.
v.c: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who responds to the distressed when they cry to Him, relieving ˹their˺ affliction, and ˹Who˺ makes you successors in the earth? Is it another god besides Allah? Yet you are hardly mindful!”

q: in the darkness of the land and sea
(by creating landmarks, the heavenly bodies and teaching you the skill of navigation. Is He not better than the gods of the Mushrikeen)?
Who sends the winds as a carrier of good news
(rain. Is He not better than the gods of the Mushrikeen)?
Is there another Ilaah with Allaah? Allaah is Exalted high above what
(as His partners). (Therefore there cannot be anyone who deserves to be worshipped with Allaah.)
v.s: Is He [not best] who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity with God? High is God above whatever they associate with Him.
v.c: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who guides you in the darkness of the land and sea, and sends the winds ushering in His mercy? Is it another god besides Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺!

q: (on the Day of Qiyaamah when people are resurrected from their graves),
and Who sustains you from the sky
(by causing all types of food to grow and other forms of life to live off it. Is He not better than the gods of the Mushrikeen)?
Is there another Ilaah with Allaah?
(There cannot be! However, if the Mushrikeen still maintain that their gods can do what Allaah does, then)
v.s: Is He [not best] who begins creation and then repeats it and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a deity with God? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."
v.c: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who originates the creation then resurrects it, and gives you provisions from the heavens and the earth? Is it another god besides Allah?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof, if what you say is true.”

q: (In addition to the powers of Allaah mentioned above)
“None in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unseen but Allaah.
(Let alone the other matters of the unseen)
do not even know when they will be resurrected.”
(This is something that none but Allaah knows.)
v.s: Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “None in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah. Nor do they know when they will be resurrected.”

q: they have no knowledge of the Aakhirah. No!
(Making matters even worse is the fact that)
They are in doubt about it
(about the coming of Qiyaamah and the Aakhirah. Therefore, they are hesitant to believe even if they are told about it).
(Making matters still worse is the fact that)
(and even lengthy explanations fail to convince them).
v.s: Rather, their knowledge is arrested concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are, concerning it, blind.
v.c: No! Their knowledge of the Hereafter amounts to ignorance. In fact, they are in doubt about it. In truth, they are ˹totally˺ blind to it.

q: say, “When our forefathers and we have turned into dust and bones
v.s: And those who disbelieve say, "When we have become dust as well as our forefathers, will we indeed be brought out [of the graves]?
v.c: The disbelievers ask, “When we and our fathers are reduced to dust, will we really be brought forth ˹alive˺?

q: “Our forefathers and we have been promised this
(long before you). (However, until now we have not seen anyone rise from his grave. This can therefore not be true. We therefore conclude that)
v.s: We have been promised this, we and our forefathers, before. This is not but legends of the former peoples."
v.c: We have already been promised this, as well as our forefathers earlier. This is nothing but ancient fables!”

q: “Travel in the lands and see what was the plight of the sinners
(see how those like you who rejected Imaan were destroyed by Allaah's punishment).'
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “Proceed [i.e., travel] through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals.”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the wicked.”

q: (about the Kuffaar rejecting Imaan because it is no fault of yours)
(against you because We shall certainly assist you).
v.s: And grieve not over them or be in distress from what they conspire.
v.c: Do not grieve for them, nor be distressed by their schemes.

q: (about it coming to us because of our kufr)?”
v.s: And they say, "When is [the fulfillment of] this promise, if you should be truthful?"
v.c: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”

q: that you seek to hurry is close behind you
v.s: Say, "Perhaps it is close behind you [i.e., very near] - some of that for which you are impatient.
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Perhaps some of what you seek to hasten is close at hand.”

q: Without doubt your Rabb is Most Bountiful towards people
(by not punishing them immediately but gives them time to repent),
but most of them are ungrateful
(and ask for the punishment instead of mending their ways).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty for the people, but most of them do not show gratitude.”
v.c: Surely your Lord is ever Bountiful to humanity, but most of them are ungrateful.

q: Indeed your Rabb knows what their hearts conceal
(state openly and He will therefore punish them when He deems that the moment is right).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
v.c: And surely your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.

q: Every hidden thing in the heavens and the earth is recorded in the clear book
(the “Lowhul Mahfoodh”). (Among the facts recorded is the time when the Kuffaar will be punished. Their punishment will neither come sooner nor later than this fixed time.)
v.s: And there is nothing concealed within the heaven and the earth except that it is in a clear Register.
v.c: For there is nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth without being ˹written˺ in a perfect Record.

q: Verily this Qur'aan relates to the Bani Israa'eel most of the matters about which they differ
v.s: Indeed, this Qur’ān relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they disagree.
v.c: Indeed, this Quran clarifies for the Children of Israel most of what they differ over.

q: guidance and mercy for the Mu'mineen
(being the last Divine message to mankind).
v.s: And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers.
v.c: And it is truly a guide and mercy for the believers.

q: Without doubt Allaah will decide between them
(the factions of the Bani Israa'eel as well as between the Mu'mineen and the Kuffaar)
(none can hide any evidence from Him).
v.s: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His [wise] judgement. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
v.c: Your Lord will certainly judge between them by His justice, for He is the Almighty, All-Knowing.

q: (for He will protect you from your enemies).
(the true Deen of Islaam and can therefore expect Allaah's assistance against your enemies).
v.s: So rely upon God; indeed, you are upon the clear truth.
v.c: So put your trust in Allah, for you are surely upon the ˹Path of˺ clear truth.

q: Verily, you cannot make the dead
(the truth because they refuse to accept),
neither can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away in aversion
(just as it is impossible to make a deaf person understand something when he refuses to even look at you, you will be unable to convince those Kuffaar who are not destined to become Muslims).
v.s: Indeed, you will not make the dead hear, nor will you make the deaf hear the call when they have turned their backs retreating.
v.c: You certainly cannot make the dead hear ˹the truth˺. Nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs and walk away.

q: You cannot guide the blind from their deviation
You can guide only those who believe in Our Aayaat and who are Muslims
(people who have submitted themselves to Allaah).
v.s: And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You will only make hear those who believe in Our verses so they are Muslims [i.e., submitting to God].
v.c: Nor can you lead the blind out of their misguidance. You can make none hear ˹the truth˺ except those who believe in Our revelations, ˹fully˺ submitting ˹to Allah˺.

q: We shall bring for them a creature from the earth, which will speak to them
are not convinced about Our Aayaat.”

(However, they will now be convinced when they see for themselves, but it will there be too late. One of the last signs before Qiyaamah will be the appearance of the “creature of the earth” who will emerge from the earth from mount Saffa after which it will make its appearance in the Masjidul Haraam. The creature will cause the faces of the Mu'mineen to shine brightly and the Mu'mineen will be clearly distinguished from the Kuffaar. Details of the creature can be found in the detailed books of Ahadeeth.)
v.s: And when the word [i.e., decree] befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith].
v.c: And when the decree ˹of the Hour˺ comes to pass against them, We will bring forth for them a beast from the earth, telling them that the people had no sure faith in Our revelations.

q: The day when, from every nation, We will resurrect
those who deny Our Aayaat, who will then be restrained
(kept in check so that they can all be led to answer before Allaah).
v.s: And [warn of] the Day when We will gather from every nation a company of those who deny Our signs, and they will be [driven] in rows
v.c: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather from every faith-community a group of those who denied Our revelations, and they will be driven in ranks.

q: Until the time will come when they will all arrive
will ask, “Did you reject My Aayaat without possessing complete knowledge
or what were the other actions that you carried out
(because of which you will have to suffer punishment today)?”
v.s: Until, when they arrive [at the place of Judgement], He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you encompassed them not in knowledge, or what [was it that] you were doing?"
v.c: When they ˹finally˺ come before their Lord, He will ask ˹them˺, “Did you deny My revelations without ˹even˺ comprehending them? Or what ˹exactly˺ did you do?”

q: will be fulfilled because of their oppression
and they will be unable to speak
(because the evidence against them will be totally convincing).
v.s: And the decree will befall them for the wrong they did, and they will not [be able to] speak.
v.c: And the decree ˹of torment˺ will be justified against them for their wrongdoing, leaving them speechless.

q: Do they not see that We have made the night so that they may rest
to see? There are certainly Aayaat
in this for those who have Imaan.
v.s: Do they not see that We made the night that they may rest therein and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
v.c: Do they not see that We made the night for them to rest in and the day bright? Surely in this are signs for those who believe.
v.h: Allah’s Power 1) The Day and Night

q: when the trumpet will be blown and all within the heavens and the earth will be terrified, but those whom Allaah wills
(those whom Allaah wishes to save will have no fear). (When people rise from the graves),
They will all come to Allaah in humility.
v.s: And [warn of] the Day the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom God wills. And all will come to Him humbled.
v.c: And ˹beware of˺ the Day the Trumpet will be blown, and all those in the heavens and all those on the earth will be horrified ˹to the point of death˺, except those Allah wills ˹to spare˺. And all will come before Him, fully humbled.

q: You will look at the mountains, thinking
but they will be passing by like clouds
(floating about in the air and eventually reduced to dust). (This is all)
The doing of Allaah Who perfects everything
(just as Allaah grants strength to weak things, so too can He weaken strong things like the mountains).
(and will take you to task for the wrong you do).
v.s: And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of God, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Acquainted with that which you do.
v.c: Now you see the mountains, thinking they are firmly fixed, but they are travelling ˹just˺ like clouds. ˹That is˺ the design of Allah, Who has perfected everything. Surely He is All-Aware of what you do.

q: from the terror of that day
(because they will not have to fear of being hurled into Jahannam).
v.s: Whoever comes [at Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe.
v.c: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded with what is better, and they will be secure from the horror on that Day.

q: on their faces in the Fire
(in the world. You therefore deserve what you are receiving and are not being oppressed in the least).”
v.s: And whoever comes with an evil deed - their faces will be overturned into the Fire, [and it will be said], "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?"
v.c: And whoever comes with an evil deed will be hurled face-first into the Fire. Are you rewarded except for what you used to do?

q: “I have been commanded to worship only the Rabb of this city
(thereby granting Him the authority to do as He pleases).
And I have been commanded to be from among the Muslims
v.s: [Say, O Muhammad], “I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who made it sacred and to whom [belongs] all things. And I am commanded to be of the Muslims [i.e., those who submit to God]
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city ˹of Mecca˺, Who has made it sacred, and to Him belongs everything. And I am commanded to be one of those who ˹fully˺ submit ˹to Him˺,

q: Whoever is rightly guided, is guided for his own benefit
(because a person's obedience to Allaah does not benefit Allaah, but benefits the person).
As for those who go astray, say
“I am only from those who warn
(I have fulfilled my duty to convey the message of islaam to you and I cannot force you to accept Imaan, I have completed my duty).”
v.s: And to recite the Qur’ān." And whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself; and whoever strays - say, "I am only [one] of the warners."
v.c: and to recite the Quran.” Then whoever chooses to be guided, it is only for their own good. But whoever chooses to stray, say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a warner.”

q: Say, “All praise is for Allaah. He will soon show you His Aayaat
Your Rabb is not unaware of what you do
(and will take you to task for the evil that you do).”
v.s: And say, "[All] praise is [due] to God. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do."
v.c: And say, “All praise is for Allah! He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is never unaware of what you do.”
